approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES language prior from the supplied unlabeled strings and selects its checkpoint using a fixed holdout. Each objective starts with a fresh policy and a frozen reference prior. The current batch elites train together with a uniform sample from the thirty-two strongest earlier accepted elites, using unchanged accepted scores and original strings. A prior-likelihood-plus-reward target drives bounded updates, and the policy directly samples complete new molecules with chemical validation and duplicate rejection. Prior training gives every token equal weight, so predictions at branch openings receive a small share of the training objective even though the observed prior makes larger errors in those contexts.
approach.novelty: Balance the unlabeled learning objective between tokens predicted immediately after an opening branch parenthesis and all remaining tokens. When both groups occur, give each group half of the total loss weight while preserving equal weights within each group. This increases the influence of a measured difficult attachment-context class without changing molecular strings, token units, model architecture or any online search rule. The earlier sibling changed bracket tokenization; this experiment tests how existing prediction errors are weighted during prior learning. Better branch-context prediction is the intermediate claim, and its effect on valid novel chemistry remains a separate experiment outcome.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-15499bde2e65 averages next-token cross entropy over all nonpadding targets during unlabeled preparation. A corpus audit using its unchanged tokenizer finds 6,032,938 targets immediately following an opening branch parenthesis among 61,472,175 targets including EOS: 9.814095564375264 percent. Their coefficient mass in each Parent minibatch is therefore only their within-batch token fraction. A read-only diagnostic of the verified seed-0 Parent checkpoint on the first 256 rows of its existing fixed holdout measures branch-entry NLL 0.8520587086677551 and top-1 accuracy 0.711357831954956 over 1,171 targets, versus NLL 0.5476776361465454 and accuracy 0.804887056350708 over 10,804 other targets. This is a measured conditional prediction gap on that subset, not proof of a corpus-wide causal search limitation. The Parent three-seed macro mean is 0.5075540530185733; its Molecular assessment reports uneven control of useful attachment patterns despite broad scaffold coverage. Sibling n-40b80eb7455d improved bracket-token context learning but had paired macro change -0.0009832613721652932, so local likelihood improvement must again be separated from actual chemical search benefit.
hypothesis: During unlabeled prior preparation, replace the uniform nonpadding token loss by an equal-weight mean of branch-entry target loss and remaining-target loss, where a branch-entry target immediately follows the input token (, while preserving the original unweighted holdout checkpoint criterion and all online learning and generation.

finding_summary.headline: Branch predictions improved in every seed, while validity and mean score fell
finding_summary.insights: The full holdouts extend the initial small probe: branch-entry prediction is a real, repeatable learning opportunity, and changing its loss allocation improves that prediction. The cost is also repeatable. Giving half the loss to roughly one-tenth of targets degrades the remaining contexts enough to worsen the ordinary language-model criterion. The observed logit-gradient movement establishes actual loss influence; it does not identify a parameter-level causal contribution to any task score. The downstream results separate branch syntax from useful attachment chemistry. Accepted scaffold variety remains broad, yet lower duplication accompanies lower validity and fewer novel raw draws. Conventional aminoquinazoline refinement can succeed locally, while the sitagliptin trajectories do not sustain favorable size, polar-group placement and nitrogen-functional-state combinations despite broad atom and ring coverage. Configurationally relevant products still lack stereochemical specification, and oversized or reactive outliers remain possible. This rules out failed loss activation and insufficient training exposure as explanations for the missing expected gain. The open question is whether context learning can preserve the much larger remaining-token group and improve useful molecular neighborhoods at the same time; improved accuracy immediately after an opening parenthesis is insufficient on its own.
finding_summary.results: The loss changed in all 89,226 preparation batches. Branch-entry targets accounted for 9.81% of 1,101,205,242 training targets; their mean assigned weight in the batch loss rose from 9.48% to 50%. All 183 registered checks showed a nonzero balanced-minus-ordinary logit-gradient change, at least 263,723 times its tolerance, with no extra optimizer steps. On the full fixed holdouts, mean branch-entry NLL fell from initialization's 4.5903 to 0.7763 nats per target. Against the paired Parent checkpoints, the mean fell from 0.8660 to 0.7763, with improvement in every seed; branch accuracy rose from 69.48% to 72.80%. Remaining-target NLL rose from 0.5318 to 0.5950, with accuracy falling from 81.32% to 79.19%; overall unweighted NLL worsened from 0.5646 to 0.6128. All preparations executed 29,742 batches, taking a mean 245.7 seconds versus 243.5 for the Parent. All 15 objectives finished with unchanged online learning and a frozen prior. Raw validity fell from 90.43% to 84.15%; duplicates fell from 30.11% to 25.61%, but novel draws also fell from 60.31% to 58.54%. The three-seed macro score fell from 0.507554 to 0.501572, a paired mean change of -0.005982. Individual seed changes were -0.016173, -0.011505 and +0.009733. Decoration hopping improved by 0.026994 on average, while sitagliptin decreased by 0.069296 and was lower in all three seeds.

molecular.headline: Conventional aromatic amide, aminoquinazoline and piperazine series, with uneven useful-core coverage and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The assessment reads all 4,500 child and 4,500 Parent trajectory rows, including 4,350 optimizer proposals per node. The child mainly produces recognizable medicinal-chemistry building blocks: aromatic amides and ureas, pyridines and pyridones, aminoquinazolines, saturated amine rings, thioethers, sulfonamides and carbonyl heterocycles. All emitted child SMILES parse in the supplied RDKit environment. Digest ring-closure marker rates are 0.9851–0.9966 and aromatic-marker rates 0.9425–0.9966; these are string-level presence readings, not aromatic atom fractions. Read-only RDKit measurements give median heavy-atom counts of 23, 27, 22, 24 and 25 in the brief task order, with a median of three rings in every set. The dominant chemistry is synthetically plausible as a class, although the trajectories establish neither routes nor physical properties and some bridged or highly elaborated examples remain difficult to assess. Direct N–halogen bonds occur in 13 of the 4,350 proposals, S–halogen bonding in one, and O–O bonds in three; unusual bonding is a minority concern here. The broader repertoire is diverse, but several leading neighborhoods repeatedly decorate one core family. Every task digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0; RDKit finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 130, 93, 457, 248 and 317 optimizer rows respectively and assigned centres in none. The main chemical limitations are therefore uneven coverage of useful core arrangements, attachment-context control, and missing configurational specification, with occasional oversized output rather than pervasive implausible chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The upper tail consists of medium-sized, largely aromatic amides, N-substituted pyridones and aminopyridyl carboxamides. The leading molecule is a benzamide with a pyridylmethyl group on its amide nitrogen and a pyridylmethoxy substituent on the benzene ring; it has 24 heavy atoms and three aromatic six-membered rings. Related molecules vary pyridine nitrogen placement or connect anisole/aniline-like groups to pyridone or pyridine-amide cores. A seed-0 example combines a sulfur/nitrogen heteroaryl amide with pyridylmethyl and hydroxyphenethyl substituents. These are generally recognizable synthetic targets, not exotic valence constructions. The child median is 23 heavy atoms and three rings, versus 24 and three in the Parent. Its 605 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, compared with 459 Parent scaffolds, reflect a varied repertoire but include local ring changes. Parent high families included indole carboxamides and diarylamino sulfonamides, so the observed change is in useful core and linker choices rather than basic availability of amide or aromatic chemistry.
liabilities: Many high examples carry three aromatic rings and flexible methylene or ether connections. Their solubility, conformational preferences and other physical properties are not measured by the supplied molecular evidence.

A few late structures introduce hydrazide or N–O-containing amide connections. These require context-specific chemical assessment rather than an assumption that every polar attachment is interchangeable.

The low tail includes substantially larger bridged or polyfunctional structures, with complicated stereochemistry left unspecified. No child proposal exceeds 50 heavy atoms, so this is an occasional within-range elaboration problem rather than pervasive size expansion.
missing_features: Alternative compact cores that preserve the useful aromatic-nitrogen/carbonyl/linker relationships are not consistently established among the high neighbors. The pool already contains varied ring systems, so a general lack of rings or amides would be an incorrect diagnosis.
Configurationally specified versions of the hydroxyalkyl amides and substituted saturated cores are absent. The trajectories do not identify a preferred stereoisomer.
Controlled changes in functional-group placement are incompletely covered: nearby heteroatom positions can remain favorable, while broader fusion and connection changes can lose much of the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The pyridylmethyl/pyridylmethoxy benzamide scores 0.4629100498862757; moving the nitrogen in its ether-linked pyridine gives 0.45115387952321717 in two cited positional alternatives. A pyridone-linked diaryl compound scores 0.45883631621439397, and its differently connected dimethylamino-containing relative scores 0.4554438514140695. The aminopyridyl carboxamide family reaches 0.44941366017785356, while a late fused quinoline carboxamide scores 0.11265354565512442. These are whole-molecule associations with specific aromatic nitrogen, carbonyl and linker arrangements, not evidence that merely adding rings or nitrogens helps. The large bridged/polyfunctional low example scores 1.238135932165025e-30, and a heavily substituted polyaryl amide scores 5.6006731847287005e-30. The digest median is 0.078725. No specific absent target heterocycle is identified by these observations.

per_task.generated_character: The digest upper tail is a focused series of fluorinated anilinoquinazolines. A fused bicyclic aza-aromatic core carries an anilino group and methoxy, fluoro, ester or related substituents; the leading example has 23 heavy atoms and three aromatic six-membered rings. Seed 2 produces more extended amino-substituted aza-aromatics with additional anilino and trifluoromethyl groups, while seed 1 includes benzyl-linked aza-lactams. These remain largely conventional, planar medicinal-chemistry motifs. The child median is 27 heavy atoms and three rings, compared with 28 and four in the Parent. Nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts are 411 versus 529, and the child digest halogen-marker rate is 0.808. The Parent high families included other aminoheteroaromatics, an acylhydrazone-containing structure and a sulfur-containing cyclic carbonyl system; the new high neighborhood is chemically more concentrated around the aminoquinazoline arrangement.
liabilities: Repeated halogenation and largely planar aromatic architectures leave physical-property balance unestablished. Small score differences do not justify treating additional fluorines or aromatic groups as chemically beneficial by themselves.
The larger late aminoaza-aromatic assemblies add multiple aromatic regions and flexible substituents without retaining the strongest observed values in the cited examples.

These leading motifs have generally plausible bond connectivity; the principal limitation visible here is concentrated useful-core coverage, rather than a dominant reactive-group or invalid-valence problem.
missing_features: Chemically distinct compact cores retaining the favorable donor/acceptor and aryl attachment pattern are underrepresented in the high excerpt; most leaders are peripheral variants of one aminoquinazoline family.

The observed series does not establish a missing required functional group. Nitrogen-rich aromatic cores, anilino donors and halogenated surfaces are present, while independent changes in their spatial arrangement remain insufficiently characterized.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The dimethoxy/difluoroanilino leader and a methoxy/fluoro core variant each score 0.6478735538536744. A methyl-substituted analogue scores 0.6476431632255552 and one trifluoroanilino positional variant scores 0.6468587434973989, while other fluorine placements give 0.637374461979914. Thus more fluorine is not a general improvement rule. Adding an ester-containing substituent gives 0.6367025683512841, and a late larger aminoaza-aromatic assembly scores 0.6039317281316672. In contrast, the compact aryl tert-butyl sulfone scores 0.2592600758444307, a sulfone/alkyne assembly 0.26495513459621134, and a differently connected diarylamino/sulfone molecule 0.31112566484083515. These observations favor the particular connected aminoaza-aromatic arrangement rather than aromaticity, fluorine or an amino group alone. The digest median is 0.559585.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-0 family is an arylpiperazine with a propyl thioether connecting the second piperazine nitrogen to another phenyl group. Fluorine/chlorine positions and linker length vary around that architecture. The leader has 23 heavy atoms and three six-membered rings, two aromatic. The sulfur is a carbon-bound thioether, not a direct nitrogen–sulfur linkage. Other seeds produce phenolic saturated amines and more elaborate bridged aryl amines. The Parent already favored related aromatic/basic-amine architectures, including arylpiperazines linked to an indole and fused amine systems. The child median is 22 heavy atoms and three rings versus 26 and four in the Parent. This set therefore contains a substantial conventional, relatively compact amine repertoire, alongside more complex late polycycles. Its charged-marker rate is 0.0552; neutral SMILES still encode accessible secondary or tertiary amines.
liabilities: Flexible carbon chains, aromatic thioethers and halogenated rings leave oxidation behavior and physical-property balance unmeasured. These are ordinary chemical concerns, not evidence that the leading structures are unmakeable.

The broader output contains unassigned tetrahedral centres in 457 of 870 proposals, with none assigned. Several quoted linear piperazine leaders are themselves achiral; the omission especially affects the branched and bridged families.

Thirteen optimizer proposals carry a direct N–halogen bond, compared with none in the corresponding Parent task. Their observed scores range from 0.0051973434795414735 to 0.9810530513457977; this minority chemistry should not be confused with the conventional carbon-bound halogens in the leading digest series.
missing_features: No further required pharmacophoric group is identifiable from the near-limit upper values: basic saturated nitrogen centres and aromatic surfaces are already present.
Stereochemically specified and geometrically controlled versions of the bridged amine output are absent. The data do not identify a preferred configuration.

Functional-group changes do not consistently retain the same amine availability and aryl/linker relationship; sulfonylation or acylation changes the nitrogen environment even when a familiar ring remains.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The chlorophenylpiperazine/phenylthiopropyl leader scores 0.9999995888205627 and the unhalogenated relative 0.999997954181706. Chlorine or fluorine on the other aromatic group each gives 0.99999794173254, and longer carbon linkers also remain close to the upper limit. These tiny differences do not identify a required halogen position or an advantage to extra linker length. By contrast, the cited arylpiperazine whose other nitrogen is sulfonylated scores 7.28002272002239e-05, and the carbamate/sulfonyl piperazine 8.983967173331926e-05. An amide-rich heteroaryl/thioether molecule scores 4.062551068938632e-05. The contrast concerns the whole accessible-amine/aryl/linker arrangement, not simply piperazine, sulfur or nitrogen presence. Late bridged amines span 0.8356123507459294 to 0.9945851759163669 among the cited examples. Parent members of the same broad amine/aromatic class already reach 0.9999999999666845, so no additional missing group can be deduced from near-limit scores.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest molecule is a bis-sulfonylated piperazine linking a methylenedioxyphenyl group and a fused aza-aromatic group. It has 31 heavy atoms and five rings, three aromatic; both piperazine nitrogens are sulfonylated, so this is not a free dibasic piperazine. Other leading molecules combine a sulfonylpiperazine with a heteroaryl amide, carbamate, pyrimidinone-like system, indole or phenolic aminopyridine. These are conventional functional-group combinations with varied aromatic and carbonyl environments. The child median is 24 heavy atoms and three rings, compared with 23 and three in the Parent, and the nonchiral Murcko counts are 768 and 755. Parent high examples already included a simple N-methyl sulfonylpiperazine, diaryl carbonyl heterocycles and fused lactam/sulfone structures. Thus broad output diversity and sulfonylated nitrogen chemistry are available; the leading relationships remain selective within that repertoire.
liabilities: The leading molecule combines two sulfonyl groups with several aromatic rings. Its polarity, lipophilicity and synthetic accessibility are not quantified by the score, although its bonding is conventional.
Repeated N-sulfonyl or N-acyl substitution changes basicity and hydrogen-bonding behavior; the familiar piperazine shape should not obscure those electronic differences.

A few highly elaborated structures occur, while most of the pool remains moderate in size. Only three of 870 child proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, and unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 248 proposals.
missing_features: Independent alternatives preserving the favorable aromatic/sulfonyl/nitrogen arrangement are not consistently populated at the leading level, despite high whole-pool scaffold diversity.

Systematic changes to the electronic state and attachment context of the piperazine nitrogens are not established as a coherent comparable series. Free amine, sulfonamide, amide and carbamate variants are chemically distinct, even though they share a ring.
The more elaborate saturated members lack explicit stereochemical specification; the leading bis-sulfonylpiperazine itself does not require an invented stereocentre.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bis-sulfonylpiperazine with fused aromatic partners scores 0.23803457280434542. The heteroaryl-amide/sulfonylpiperazine scores 0.2049217645670816, the anilino carbonyl-azaheterocycle 0.20035810234584286 and the carbamate/benzodioxane-sulfonylpiperazine 0.19980516312959098. A late bis-sulfonylpiperazine with differently substituted chlorophenyl groups scores 0.17026918875314892. The nitrogen ring and sulfonyl groups are therefore insufficient by themselves; the aromatic and polar-group arrangement matters. A flexible isoprenoid-like alcohol scores 0.015382535047175145, an allyl glycoside 0.019109830873967712, and a urea connecting bulky saturated polycycles 0.028162869316208303. These low examples show that either oxygen abundance or saturated ring bulk alone fails to reproduce the favorable aromatic/sulfonyl/nitrogen pattern. The digest median is 0.12365; the trajectories do not identify a unique missing target fragment.

per_task.generated_character: The leading examples span several unrelated compact families. Seed 0 provides a hydroxy-substituted fused conjugated diaza system attached to a bridged saturated nitrogen/sulfur core; it has 20 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, with two unassigned tetrahedral centres. Seed 2 supplies a methylcarboxamide on a sulfur/nitrogen five-membered heteroaromatic ring bearing phenyl and an N-mesylpyrrolidine. Other high examples include an imino-substituted methoxy/ester indene-like system, a diaryl nitrogen tricarbonyl ring and spiro hydantoin-like carbonyl structures. Most individual functional groups are familiar, but the leading bridged arrangement and imine-containing conjugated systems are less straightforward synthetic propositions than simple amides. The child median is 25 heavy atoms and three rings versus 24 and three in the Parent. Parent leaders included sulfonamide/carbonyl heteroaromatics, a dimethylamino acetanilide bearing another amide, and a fused imino/dicarbonyl system. Useful chemistry is therefore dispersed across distinct families rather than missing nitrogen or carbonyl groups in general.
liabilities: The leading bridged core has unassigned stereochemistry, and its exact geometry and synthetic route are unestablished. Imine, hydrazide, thioamide and spiro carbonyl variants elsewhere in the high set need individual chemical interpretation.

The output occasionally expands into large lipid/peptide/polyol assemblies. Thirteen of 870 child proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, compared with four Parent proposals; the maximum child heavy-atom count is 82.

Carbonyl-rich or heavily substituted late molecules often lose the favorable whole-molecule arrangement. Their familiar individual groups do not by themselves establish appropriate physicochemical balance.
missing_features: Chemically coherent neighboring variants around the several favorable compact families are insufficiently represented; high raw scaffold variety does not establish useful coverage of the local nitrogen/carbonyl/aromatic arrangements.
Explicit configurations of the bridged nitrogen/sulfur system and substituted pyrrolidine are absent. The evidence does not establish which configuration would help.

Size and substitution changes that retain useful polar-group placement remain inconsistent. The data do not support a generic instruction to add a primary amine, fluorine or one named heterocycle, because the favorable examples are chemically different.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bridged nitrogen/sulfur–diaza structure scores 0.24814859991786153, the heteroaryl carboxamide/N-mesylpyrrolidine 0.22792078190126805, the imino/ester indene-like structure 0.21139786454760395 and the diaryl tricarbonyl nitrogen ring 0.20781853886196197. No one functional group is common enough across these examples to infer a uniquely required absent feature. A cyclic sulfonimide attached through an amide chain to anilide scores 0.18284253097618777, whereas its late dibenzyl-substituted amide relative scores 1.2579028785661194e-07, associating excessive substitution and changed amide context with a sharp loss in that family. Large peptide-like, lipid-like and polyol-rich assemblies include six exact zero scores among the 900 rows. The digest displays median 0.0 because of its precision; the actual median over those rows is 2.002143064293774e-08, and the optimizer-only median is 2.159983702231957e-08. These are predominantly tiny positive values rather than a claim that most evaluations are exactly zero. The breadth of sampled cores has not translated into dense coverage of favorable local arrangements.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Aryl piperazines with an alkyl thioether linker score near the upper limit, whereas a sulfonylated arylpiperazine scores 7.28002272002239e-05 in the same trajectory set. In another set, a bis-sulfonylpiperazine scores 0.23803457280434542, so sulfonylation is not uniformly undesirable. A carbonyl-chain anilide scores 0.18284253097618777 while its more heavily substituted dibenzyl amide relative scores 1.2579028785661194e-07. The observations distinguish whole-molecule attachment context rather than presence or absence of a familiar group.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful functional-group placement and electronic context are not consistently preserved while exploring familiar molecular frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent free amines, aryl amines, amides, sulfonamides and carbamates as distinct chemical environments when varying attachment points and linkers. Preserve useful surrounding donor, acceptor and aromatic relationships during local changes, and let the current session accepted observations determine which electronic and spatial arrangement matters.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The child has 605, 411, 506, 768 and 772 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds across the supplied sets, but its upper excerpts repeatedly decorate pyridyl amides, aminoquinazolines, arylpiperazines and sulfonylpiperazines. A different set has several unrelated compact high examples while its raw 900-row median is only 2.002143064293774e-08. These counts demonstrate variety, not a comparable number of useful scaffold neighborhoods.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad overall scaffold variety does not ensure sustained coverage of chemically useful local core families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Retain access to multiple accepted core families and populate chemically coherent neighbors that preserve their useful local functional-group relationships. Distinguish genuinely different core chemistry from peripheral decoration or a new molecular string, and balance exploring new families with developing the ones supported by accepted feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest has stereocentre_rate 0.0. Read-only RDKit checks identify unassigned tetrahedral centres in 130, 93, 457, 248 and 317 optimizer rows in the brief task order and assigned centres in none. The cited hydroxyalkyl amide, bridged aryl amines, nitrogen/sulfur bicyclic core and substituted pyrrolidine illustrate configurationally relevant output; several linear aromatic/piperazine leaders are achiral and should not be assigned artificial centres.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemistry even when it generates substituted saturated and bridged structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit, chemically valid configurations for existing stereogenic centres and geometrically coherent variants of saturated or bridged rings. Keep configuration changes distinct from changes in connectivity so accepted feedback can compare actual stereochemical alternatives. The missing representation does not establish a benefit for any chosen configuration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Most child sets have median heavy-atom counts between 22 and 27 and no proposals with at most three heavy atoms. Nevertheless, one set produces 13 structures above 50 heavy atoms versus four in its Parent, with large lipid/peptide/polyol assemblies among the exact-zero examples. A cited heavily substituted dibenzyl amide scores 1.2579028785661194e-07 where a simpler anilide family member scores 0.18284253097618777. The gap is selective over-elaboration, not pervasive fragmentation or a universal need to minimize size.
transferable_gaps.gap: Occasional large or heavily substituted outputs lose useful compact arrangements despite generally moderate molecular size.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide growth, contraction and linker choices that retain the accepted core and its useful local polar-group arrangement. Use feedback to determine how much substitution a family tolerates, without repeatedly expanding into unrelated large assemblies or assuming that either more complexity or smaller size is always better.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

Unlabeled preparation gives branch-entry and remaining next-token contexts one-half loss mass each when both groups occur, retains the ordinary single-group fallback, and preserves unweighted original-holdout checkpoint selection with conditional and logit-gradient diagnostics.
